using Base64
using Statistics

function main()
    # Read all input from stdin
    content = read(stdin, String)
    if isempty(content)
        print("Error: Empty input\n")
        exit(1)
    end

    # Parse CSV
    lines = split(content, '\n', keephead=true)
    if isempty(lines)
        print("Error: No data found\n")
        exit(1)
    end

    # Get header
    header = split(lines[1], ',')
    if isempty(header)
        print("Error: Invalid header\n")
        exit(1)
    end

    # Get data rows
    data_rows = [split(line, ',') for line in lines[2:end]]
    if isempty(data_rows)
        print("Error: No data rows\n")
        exit(1)
    end

    # Check if last column exists
    last_col_idx = length(header)
    if last_col_idx <= 0
        print("Error: No columns\n")
        exit(1)
    end

    # Extract values from the last column
    values = Float64[]
    for row in data_rows
        if length(row) >= last_col_idx
            val_str = row[last_col_idx]
            # Try to parse as Float64, ignoring invalid values
            try
                val = parse(Float64, val_str)
                push!(values, val)
            catch
                # Ignore invalid values
                continue
            end
        end
    end

    # Check if we have enough valid values for skewness (need at least 3)
    if length(values) < 3
        print("Error: Not enough valid numeric values to compute skewness\n")
        exit(1)
    end

    # Compute skewness
    mean_val = mean(values)
    std_val = std(values)

    if std_val == 0
        # If standard deviation is zero, skewness is undefined or zero depending on definition
        # Using the common definition: E[((X-mu)/sigma)^3]
        # If all values are the same, the term inside is always 1, so mean is 1
        # However, some definitions set it to 0 if std is 0. 
        # The standard Julia Statistics skewness returns NaN if std is 0.
        # Let's replicate the behavior of Statistics.skewness which returns NaN if std is 0.
        skewness = NaN
    else
        skewness = skewness(values)
    end

    # Print result
    print(skewness)
end
